lines: A game of pong whose ball, paddles and bounces are all available as triggers and control voltage
Sets player 1's paddle position, 0-10V from one end of the screen to the other, in place of the P1 knob
Sets player 2's paddle position, 0-10V from one end of the screen to the other, in place of the P2 knob
Sets player 1's paddle height, 0-10V from a small bat to the full height of the screen, in place of its size knob
Sets player 2's paddle height, 0-10V from a small bat to the full height of the screen, in place of its size knob
Sets the angle a new ball is served at, 0-10V covering a whole turn; with nothing patched each serve takes a random angle
Sets the height a new ball is served at, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom; with nothing patched each serve is at a random height
A rising edge above 2V serves a new ball
The clock: the ball moves one step on each rising edge, so this jack sets the pace of the game
Sets how far the ball travels on each clock step, 0-10V; with nothing patched it moves a hundredth of the screen per step
Sets player 1's paddle position; a cable in the P1 input takes over from this knob
Sets player 2's paddle position; a cable in the P2 input takes over from this knob
Sets player 1's paddle height; a cable in its size input takes over from this knob
Sets player 2's paddle height; a cable in its size input takes over from this knob
Switches between serving a new ball the moment one is lost and serving only on a trigger at the BALL input; the button reads AUTO or GATE
The ball's horizontal position, 0-10V from the left wall to the right
The ball's vertical position, 0-10V from the top of the screen to the bottom
A trigger each time the ball crosses the centre line after a paddle has sent it away
The height at which the ball last crossed the centre line, 0-10V
A trigger each time the ball strikes player 1's paddle
A trigger each time the ball strikes player 2's paddle
A trigger each time the ball goes past player 1 and off the left of the screen
A trigger each time the ball goes past player 2 and off the right of the screen
A trigger each time the ball bounces off the top of the screen
A trigger each time the ball bounces off the bottom of the screen
Where along player 1's paddle the ball last struck, 0V at the near end and 10V at the far end
Where along player 2's paddle the ball last struck, 0V at the near end and 10V at the far end
The height at which the ball last went off the left of the screen, 0-10V
The height at which the ball last went off the right of the screen, 0-10V
Where along the top of the screen the ball last bounced, 0-10V from left to right
Where along the bottom of the screen the ball last bounced, 0-10V from left to right, although the maker's tooltip on this jack reads top wall cv
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched: the ball advances one step for each rising edge at the CLK input.
Note — a trigger output is only pulsed while a cable is patched to it, and each CV output holds its last value until the same event happens again.
Note — striking the ball with a moving paddle bends its path; the faster the paddle travels, the more the angle changes.

lines: A melody generator that learns which note follows which from what you play it, then walks that map to make new melodies of the same shape
A gate here switches learning on and off, adding to whatever the record button is set to
A gate here removes the note the module is on from the map, with every link into it
Adds to the randomness knob, a tenth of a unit per volt over its travel from -1 to 1
The note to learn or to jump to, as a 1V/octave pitch
A gate marks a note at the cv input: while learning it is added to the map, and otherwise the module jumps to the learned note nearest it
A rising edge moves on to a next note, drawn from the notes that were played after the current one
Sets how closely the next note follows what was taught: at -1 the most frequent follower every time, at 0 the taught proportions, and towards +1 the rarer followers and jumps elsewhere in the map
Switches learning on and off; while it is on, a gate at the gate input adds the note at the cv input to the map
Removes the note the module is on from the map, with every link into it
The note the module is on, as a 1V/octave pitch
A gate that is high whenever the trigger input is high, and drops for the single sample a trigger arrives on so that each new note reads as a new gate
Menu — dehumanize — draws the panel plain instead of as a figure
Menu — face wiggle — lets the drawn face move as the randomness setting changes
Menu — never change clothes — keeps the drawn figure's clothing fixed
Note — the map starts empty, so the module puts out nothing until you switch learning on and play notes into the cv and gate inputs.
Note — the grid above the knob shows every note learned so far with the current one picked out; it cannot be edited.
Note — the learned map is saved with the patch.

lines: A rotating sequential switch: eight holes on an inner ring and eight on an outer ring turn past one another, and a hole is connected to the holes it comes within range of
Sets how many holes on the inner ring are in use, 1 to 8
Sets how many holes on the outer ring are in use, 1 to 8
One of the eight holes on the inner ring: an input by default, feeding whichever holes on the outer ring have come within range of it, and switched to an output by right-clicking its button
One of the eight holes on the outer ring: an output by default, carrying whatever the inner-ring holes in range of it are sending, and switched to an input by right-clicking its button
Adds to the inner ring count knob, seven holes over the full 0-10V
Adds to the outer ring count knob, seven holes over the full 0-10V
Turns the whole inner ring, -10V to 10V carrying it one full turn backwards to one full turn forwards
Turns the whole outer ring, -10V to 10V carrying it one full turn backwards to one full turn forwards
Chooses which saved snapshot of ring positions and ranges is in use, 0-10V spread across the snapshots that exist
Menu — hints — draws the on-panel prompts explaining what each gesture does
Menu — digits — numbers the holes on the drawing
Menu — animate — redraws the rings as they turn rather than only when something changes
Menu — audio-rate pairing — works out which holes are paired every sample instead of every few, which costs a lot more processing and is only needed when ring positions are modulated at audio rate
Menu — auto-equalize — spreads the holes evenly around a ring again whenever the number in use changes
Note — the working mode is chosen by clicking a letter of the word ATOMS on the panel: A, T, M and S each select one, and O selects the snapshot CV.
Note — in attack mode, chosen with the A of ATOMS, a connection fades in over a few milliseconds so that switching does not click; it is the mode to use for audio.
Note — in trigger mode, chosen with the T of ATOMS, an input hole with no cable counts as a steady 10V, which turns the rings into a gate sequencer with nothing patched in.
Note — in mixer mode, chosen with the M of ATOMS, every input in range is summed into the output with its level set by how close the two holes are; it costs the most processing of the four.
Note — in sample mode, chosen with the S of ATOMS, an output holds the last voltage it was given when its connection is lost rather than dropping to 0V.
Note — right-click a ring to switch between dragging the holes to new positions and dragging them to set how far each one reaches; the reach is drawn as an arc.
Note — the e- and e+ buttons spread the holes of a ring evenly; right-clicking one adds or removes a snapshot of the whole arrangement, and the small knob at the centre selects between the snapshots.
Note — a hole beyond the number in use can be turned into a modulation port: drag from it onto a hole to have it drive that hole's position or reach, or read out the distance to its partner as 0-10V.
Note — the maker marks this module as an alpha version in its own menu.

lines: A gate machine built on a binary tree in the shape of the Cantor set: five rows each split in two again and again, with a gate for every cell and a ratio setting how the splits fall
The phase for this row, a rising 0-10V ramp reading as one pass along the row; with nothing patched the row follows the row above it, and the first row follows the last
Adds to this row's ratio slider, a tenth of its travel per volt
Sets where this row's cells are split, and with them every row below it; at the centre the split is even
Switches this cell on and off, so a phase passing through it does or does not raise the row's gate output
The phase reached inside this row's current cell, 0-10V, while its gate is open, and 0V while it is not
10V while the phase for this row is inside a cell that is switched on, 0V otherwise
Menu — animate mods — redraws the tree as the ratio modulation moves rather than only when a slider is turned
Menu — update cycle — sets how many samples pass between one recalculation and the next, 1 to 1024; a higher number costs less processing and coarsens the gate timing
Note — nothing happens until a rising ramp is patched to a phase input; a row with no ramp of its own copies the row above it, and the first row copies the last.
Note — the button at the bottom of the panel switches the display between the ratio sliders and the gate cells; the sliders are hidden while the cells are shown.
Note — click a cell to switch it, drag across cells to set a run of them at once, and double-click a cell to switch every cell in the row below it to that setting.
Note — a polyphonic ramp at a phase input gives a polyphonic gate and phase output with one channel per ramp.
Note — the six gate inputs and the relative-mode switch are declared in the code but have no jack or button on the panel, and relative mode is left switched off.

The widget places them in the order 0, 2, 5, 1, 3, 4 (avoider.cpp:678), so the panel reads 6, 1, 2 on the upper row and 3, 4, 5 on the lower, and the tags must come from the parameter ids rather than from the layout.
